:::{#exm-gradient-linear-approximation}
#### The linear approximation of the derivative of a cubic at $x = -2.5$

For $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$, with $f'(x) = x^2 - 4$ and $f''(x) = 2x$ (@exm-newton-method),
$p = 1$, so the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) at $x = -2.5$ is the tangent line to $f'$ there:

$$
\ba
\ell(\step)
&= f'(-2.5) + f''(-2.5)\,\step
&& \text{(@eq-gradient-linear-approximation with } p = 1 \text{)}
\\
&= \paren{(-2.5)^2 - 4} + 2 (-2.5)\,\step
&& \text{(substitute } f' \text{ and } f'' \text{)}
\\
&= 2.25 - 5 \step.
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-gradient-linear-approximation-cubic}

@fig-gradient-linear-approximation graphs $f'$ and $\ell$.
